title: Length of Stay, outcome and prognostic factors of Patients with Prolonged Weaning in Neurological Early Rehabilitation Phase B
summary:
Neurological early rehabilitation Phase B is a specialized form of rehabilitation for severely ill patients following severe brain injury or other neurological and non-neurological conditions. It begins immediately after acute treatment in the hospital.
This patient group requires a particularly high level of medical care. They often remain in the hospital longer, experience more frequent complications, sometimes require further surgeries, and are treated collaboratively by various medical specialties. Intensive care is often still necessary even after discharge.
To better understand which factors influence the healing process, existing patient data will be analyzed. The goal of this analysis is to identify factors that will allow for a more accurate assessment of recovery and prognosis in the future.
conditions: Patients on ventilators, inpatient stay for early neurological rehabilitation

interventions.name: Retrospective data collection from existing datasets collected as part of routine clinical practice between 2014 and 2024: length of hospital stay/ICU stay, complications requiring readmission to intensive care, duration of ventilation, surgical procedures, swallowing assessments (FEES, swallowing k

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Compliance with OPS Code 8-552
- Tracheotomy
- Prolonged weaning
Exclusion criteria:
- Duration of treatment < 7days
